```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| include: false

library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

h1Data <- read.csv("Data/processed_data/h1Data.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("Data/processed_data/h2Data.csv")

h1Data$Gender_new <- factor(
  h1Data$Gender_new,
  levels = c("Male_Intersex", "Female")
)
```

## Hypothesis 1:

Females report higher love intensity than males and intersex respondents combined.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

-   **Binary Sex at birth (`Gender_new`):** A categorical variable with two groups: Male and intersex, female.
-   **Intensity of Love Feelings (`Love_how_much_1`):** A single item asking "How much do you love this person?" Responses range from 0 (Very little) to 100 (Very much)

```{r}
#| label: h1-descriptives
# Count respondents in each group.
table(h1Data$Gender_new)

# Summarize attractiveness points separately for each group.
by(h1Data$Love_how_much_1, h1Data$Gender_new, summary)
```

### Graph

@fig-love_intensity shows the distribution of points by binary sex at birth. The half-violin shows the shape of the distribution, the box summarize the median and quartiles, and the dots represent individual responses.

```{r}
#| label: fig-love_intensity
#| fig-cap: "Points allocated to people's love intensity, by binary sex at birth."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h1Data, aes(x = Gender_new, y = Love_how_much_1,
                   fill = Gender_new)) +
  geom_rain(alpha = 0.5, point.args = list(alpha = 0.04, size = 0.6)) +
  labs(x = "Binary Sex at birth", y = "Points allocated to people's love intensity") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Hypothesis 2:

Greater willingness to marry without romantic love is associated with lower relationship satisfaction.

### Variables and descriptive statistics

-   **Matrimonial Directedness/Marry Without Love(`Love_would_you_marry_1`):** A single item asking respondents to imagine being outside a committed relationship and meeting someone who has all their desired qualities but whom they do not love. Responses range from 0 (I would definitely not marry this person) to 100 (I would definitely marry this person)

```{=html}
<!-- -->
```
-   **Relationship satisfaction (`satisfaction`):** The mean of available responses to `prqc_1`, `prqc_2`, and `prqc_3`, which assess how satisfied, content, and happy respondents are with their relationship. Each item ranges from 1 (Not at all) to 7 (Extremely). Higher mean scores indicate greater relationship satisfaction.

```{r}
#| label: h2-descriptives
summary(h2Data[, c("Love_would_you_marry_1", "satisfaction")])

```

### Graph

@fig-satisfaction shows the relationship between marry without love and relationship satisfaction. Points are jittered to make overlapping responses easier to see; the recorded scores are unchanged. The line summarizes the linear trend.

```{r}
#| label: fig-satisfaction
#| fig-cap: "Confidence in finding a new partner and relationship commitment."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

ggplot(h2Data, aes(x = Love_would_you_marry_1, y = satisfaction)) +
  geom_jitter(width = .12, height = .04, alpha = .04, size = .6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Marry Without Love (0–100)",
       y = "Relationship Satisfaction (1–7)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Observed trend

```{r}
#| label: correlation
r <- cor(h2Data$Love_would_you_marry_1, h2Data$satisfaction, use = "complete.obs")
round(r, 2) 
```

The correlation was `-0.06`, indicating a very weak negative association. Respondents who have greater willingness to marry without love tend to report lower relationship satisfaction.
